# Dashboards in the QuestDB Web Console (MCP)

The preferred way to build QuestDB dashboards is a **Web Console notebook**,
authored by the agent through the QuestDB MCP server. Notebooks combine SQL,
markdown and charts, refresh live per cell, take variables and a time range,
and need no extra service (no Grafana, no datasource, no plugin). Use Grafana
only when the user asks for it (see `grafana.md`).

Docs: `https://questdb.com/docs/getting-started/web-console/mcp-server.md`,
`.../web-console/notebooks/overview.md` (also `cells`, `charts`, `variables`,
`live-dashboards`, `manage-share`).

---

## Setup and Pairing

Install once (Node.js required). The wizard detects Claude Code, Codex,
Cursor, OpenCode and Gemini CLI and writes their MCP config:

```bash
npx @questdb/mcp-server-questdb@latest setup
```

The console shows the exact pinned version to use in its MCP status pill.
The old package name `@questdb/mcp-bridge` is obsolete. Manual config
(`.mcp.json` in the project root):

```json
{"mcpServers":{"questdb":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@questdb/mcp-server-questdb@latest"]}}}
```

The Web Console must be open in a browser (default `http://127.0.0.1:9000`,
override with the `CONSOLE_ORIGIN` env var). Pairing, every session:

1. Call `get_pairing_credentials`.
2. Show its `userMessage` to the user **verbatim** (deep link plus ws_url and
   token). Never skip this.
3. In the same turn call `wait_for_pairing`; it blocks up to 50 s. Retry on
   `timeout` up to about 10 times.

Unpaired tools return `BRIDGE_NOT_PAIRED`. The user picks a permission level
in the console:

| Level | Schema tools | `run_query` returns rows | DDL/DML |
|-------|--------------|--------------------------|---------|
| None | no | no | no |
| Schema access | yes | no | no |
| Read | yes | yes | no |
| Write | yes | yes | yes (only via `run_cell`, after user consent) |

Notebook authoring works at every level. Drawing or running DQL cells never
needs `read`: the user sees the data, the agent does not. If a tool returns
`PERMISSION_DENIED`, tell the user which scope to grant.

---

## Tools You Will Use

Discover data: `get_tables`, `get_table_schema`, `get_table_details`,
`validate_query` (validate every query before putting it in a cell),
`get_questdb_toc` / `get_questdb_documentation`, `run_query` (returns rows,
needs `read`).

Workspace and notebooks: `get_workspace_state` (call first in every notebook
turn; a freshness gate applies), `create_notebook(label)` (always opens in the
background), `activate_notebook` / `activate_tab` (only after the user agrees),
`duplicate_notebook`, `get_notebook_state`, `list_cells`, `get_cell`.

Tabs (newer consoles): `rename_tab`, `archive_tab` (close, reversible),
`restore_tab`, `delete_tab` (permanent, only when the user asks). Older
consoles have `delete_notebook` instead. Use whichever your tool list shows.

Cells: `add_cell`, `update_cell`, `delete_cell`, `move_cell_up/down`,
`duplicate_cell`, `run_cell`, `set_cell_name` (also the chart title),
`set_cell_mode` (`run` = table, `draw` = chart), `set_cell_chart_config`,
`set_cell_highlight_config`, `set_cell_autorefresh`,
`set_notebook_autorefresh`, `set_layout_mode`, `set_cell_layout`,
`set_cell_dimensions`, `set_cell_maximized`.

**Build a whole dashboard with one `apply_notebook_state` call.** It is a full
PUT of the notebook: cells, names, modes, chart configs, highlight rules, grid
positions, per-cell refresh, variables and the refresh default.

### Rules That Bite

- `apply_notebook_state.cells` is the COMPLETE list. Existing cells you omit
  are deleted. Omitting `chart_config` removes a chart; `name: null` clears a
  name. Use `preserve_value: true` for cells whose SQL you are not changing.
- Never write back a truncated value (`get_cell` caps at 4 KB unless
  `get_full_content: true`; previews are 120 chars).
- `chart_config.queries` must have exactly one entry per `;`-separated
  statement in the cell, or the call is rejected.
- Candlesticks need an explicit `ohlc: {open, high, low, close}` mapping.
- Draw cells auto-execute. Do not call `run_cell` after setting draw mode.
  In a background tab they render when the user opens it: `runs[]` lists only
  run-mode cells, and draw cells report `last_run_status: "none"` until then.
  Validate chart SQL with `run_query` (one statement per call; a cell's
  `;`-separated statements one at a time) before applying.
- DDL/DML is never auto-run or auto-refreshed. Create tables and views with
  `run_query` (write scope) or a cell the user runs, not in a dashboard cell.
- **Nothing polls until a refresh value is set.** Set
  `auto_refresh_default` (or `set_notebook_autorefresh`) on every live
  dashboard.
- Grid layout is 12 columns: `grid: {x, y, w}` with `w` 1-12. Height comes
  from `editor_height` / `result_height` (charts need `result_height` >= 296,
  tables >= 100). Use `view: "result"` to hide editors on a dashboard; never
  send `view: "editor"` to an existing cell, it discards its result.
- Markdown cells: `type: "markdown"`, the value is markdown, `mode` and
  `chart_config` must be null. `editor_height: 86` gives a clean title cell.
- Limits: 200 cells per notebook, 100 tabs, 10,000 rows per statement.

---

## Charts

A draw-mode cell can hold several `;`-separated SELECTs. They **combine into
one chart** sharing the first query's x-axis (all temporal: merged by time;
all categorical: merged by category). Each query has its own config:

```json
{"type": "candlestick", "y_columns": null,
 "ohlc": {"open": "open", "high": "high", "low": "low", "close": "close"},
 "partition_by_column": null, "axis": null, "enabled": null, "name": "OHLC 15m"}
```

- `type`: `line`, `area`, `stepLine`, `stepArea`, `bar`, `stackedBar`,
  `scatter`, `pie`, `candlestick`. `pie`, `scatter` and `stackedBar` render
  only as single-query charts.
- `y_columns`: columns to plot (null = all numeric). Not used for candlestick.
- `partition_by_column`: one series per value of a categorical column
  (e.g. one line per table or symbol) without pivoting in SQL.
- `axis: "right"` puts the query on the shared secondary axis;
  `right_axis: {name, min, max}` pins its title and range. Newer consoles
  also have `left_axis: {name, min, max}`.
- A **numeric** `x_column` (not a timestamp) gives a continuous value axis,
  used for depth charts and histograms.
- Newer consoles accept a `volume` column on a candlestick query, drawn as a
  sub-pane under the candles. Use it when the schema offers it; otherwise use
  the right-axis trick below.

### Highlight Rules (run-mode grids)

`set_cell_highlight_config` colors live tables:
- `kind: "previous"` + `identity_columns: ["symbol"]` flashes cells that moved
  up (`op: "gt"`, `color: "green"`) or down (`op: "lt"`, `color: "red"`).
- `kind: "value"`, `op: "between"`, `fill: "gradient"`, `value`/`to` null:
  shade a column across its current min..max.
  The gradient is linear, so on heavy-tailed columns (trade notional, order
  size) one outlier takes the far color and every other cell looks the same.
- `kind: "steps"`: thresholds, e.g. book level 1 green, 2-3 amber, 4+ red.
  Prefer steps for skewed values (notional `1000` / `10000` / `100000`).
- `kind: "newRow"`: paint rows that just appeared.
- Colors: red, teal, amber, lime, orange, purple, green, pink, blue, olive.

---

## Variables and Time Range

Notebook variables are sent to the server as a `DECLARE` block prepended to
each SELECT (merged with a cell's own `DECLARE`; the cell's names win).
Reference them as `@name`. They are not injected into INSERT/CREATE/ALTER.

```json
"variables": [
  {"name": "symbol", "value": "'EURUSD'"},
  {"name": "asof",   "value": "now()"}
]
```

- Names have no `@`. Values are raw SQL expressions: quote strings yourself
  (`"'EURUSD'"`), `now()`, `dateadd('d', -7, now())`, `'$now-1h..$now'`.
- Order matters: a variable may reference earlier ones.
- A value list works with `IN`: `{"name": "syms", "value": "('EURUSD','GBPUSD')"}`
  then `WHERE symbol IN @syms`.
- The console prepends the `DECLARE` only when its own parser accepts the
  cell. Some SQL the server accepts makes that parser fail, and the cell then
  fails with a misleading `Invalid column: @name` or, if it declares its own
  default for the variable, silently runs with that default. In cells that
  use variables, avoid:
  - SQL keywords as CTE names, table aliases or column aliases: `lt`, `asof`,
    `sample`, `splice`, `horizon`, `window`. Use `fills_lt`,
    `horizon_sec`, or quote them (`"lt"`).
  - A subquery on the right of a HORIZON JOIN, `(quotes WHERE ...)` or
    `(SELECT ...)`. Filter the right side in `ON` instead:
    `ON (t.symbol = q.symbol AND q.source = 'ICE')`.

**Newer consoles** (check the `apply_notebook_state` schema for `kind`,
`time_range` and `set_cell_time_range`) add:
- Typed variables: `kind: "expression"` (fixed SQL), `"text"` (textbox the
  user edits, inserted as written), `"list"` (picker fed by a query or a typed
  list; multi-select renders `(v1, v2)` for `IN @name`; optional "All").
- **Global variables** shared by every notebook: `get_global_variables`,
  `apply_global_variables(variables, expected_revision, time_range)`. Names
  are unique across globals and notebook variables, ignoring case. The call
  replaces the whole ordered list, so read first and pass the revision.
- A **notebook time range** (`time_range: {from, to}` with Grafana-style
  bounds such as `now-15m`, `now/d`, `now-1d/d`, or ISO timestamps) that
  declares `@timeFrom`, `@timeTo` and `@timeFilter` for every cell:
  `WHERE ts IN @timeFilter`. These three names are reserved.
- Per-cell `time_range` override and `time_shift` (e.g. `-1d` to show
  yesterday next to today), via `set_cell_time_range` or bulk apply.

When the console has no time-range support, drive ranges with plain variables
(`@asof`, `@lookback`) as in the FX example below.

---

## Refresh Per Cell

Give each cell the cadence its data deserves, and set a notebook default:

| Cell | Refresh |
|------|---------|
| Order book depth, top of book | `200ms`-`250ms` |
| 1-minute candles on 1s bars, spread table | `500ms` |
| Hourly indicators, intraday VWAP/RSI | `30s` |
| Instance metrics (`sys.metrics`) | `15s`-`1m` |

Values: `true` (adaptive), `false` (off), or `"<n>ms|s|m"` from 50ms to 60m.
Charts poll only while visible and the tab is in the foreground.

---

## Reference Dashboards (complete, working exports)

Two full notebook exports ship with this skill. Read them when building a
similar dashboard, and copy their SQL, chart configs, refresh intervals and
layout:

- `examples/fx-live-dashboard.json`: live FX order book dashboard for the
  `demo.questdb.io` dataset (depth chart, OHLC + volume overlay, indicators,
  highlighted live tables).
- `examples/monitoring-dashboard.json`: instance health from `sys.metrics`
  and `sys.telemetry_wal` (25 cells).

Structure: `data.data[0].rows[0]` is the tab (`label`), and
`notebookViewState` holds `cells[]` (`value` = SQL or markdown, `name`,
`type`, `mode`, `chartConfig`, `highlightConfig`, `autoRefresh`) and
`settings` (`layout[]` grid positions keyed by cell id, `variables[]`,
`autoRefreshDefault`). The export uses camelCase (`xColumn`, `yColumns`,
`rightAxis`, `partitionByColumn`); the MCP tools take the same fields in
snake_case (`x_column`, `y_columns`, `right_axis`, `partition_by_column`).
The user can also import either file directly: tab bar menu > **Import tabs**.

## Pattern: Live FX Dashboard (demo dataset)

Works against `demo.questdb.io` tables `market_data` (2D `bids`/`asks`
arrays), `core_price`, `bbo_1s`, `bbo_1h`, `market_data_ohlc_1m`,
`market_data_ohlc_15m`. Variables: `symbol := 'EURUSD'`, `asof := now()`.
Setting `asof` to a past timestamp replays the whole dashboard at that moment,
which is why the filters are written relative to `@asof`
(`timestamp >= dateadd('m', -1, @asof) AND timestamp <= @asof`) instead of
`$now`.

Grid layout (w=6 halves), notebook default `250ms`.

**1. Market depth, constant width (stepArea, numeric x, 200ms).** Cumulative
depth for 7 levels per side, x in pips from mid. Two extra points at
`±edge` (10 level spacings) carrying the level-7 depth keep the x-range
fixed, so the chart does not jump in width on every refresh.

```sql
WITH book AS (
  SELECT bids, asks FROM market_data
  WHERE symbol = @symbol AND timestamp >= dateadd('m', -10, @asof) AND timestamp <= @asof
  LATEST ON timestamp PARTITION BY symbol
), m0 AS (
  SELECT (bids[1][1] + asks[1][1]) / 2 AS mid,
         CASE WHEN @symbol LIKE '%JPY' THEN 0.01 WHEN @symbol = 'XAGUSD' THEN 0.001
              WHEN @symbol LIKE 'X%' THEN 0.01 ELSE 0.0001 END AS pip,
         bids[1][1] - bids[1][2] AS spacing,
         array_cum_sum(bids[2])[7] AS bid7, array_cum_sum(asks[2])[7] AS ask7
  FROM book
), m AS (
  SELECT mid, pip, round(10 * spacing / pip) AS edge, bid7, ask7 FROM m0
)
SELECT round((u.price - m.mid) / m.pip, 1) AS pips_from_mid, u.depth AS bid_depth, NULL::double AS ask_depth
FROM book b CROSS JOIN m, UNNEST(b.bids[1], array_cum_sum(b.bids[2])) WITH ORDINALITY u(price, depth, lvl)
WHERE u.lvl <= 7
UNION ALL
SELECT round((u.price - m.mid) / m.pip, 1), NULL::double, u.depth
FROM book b CROSS JOIN m, UNNEST(b.asks[1], array_cum_sum(b.asks[2])) WITH ORDINALITY u(price, depth, lvl)
WHERE u.lvl <= 7
UNION ALL SELECT -edge, bid7, NULL::double FROM m
UNION ALL SELECT edge, NULL::double, ask7 FROM m
ORDER BY pips_from_mid
```
`chart_config`: `x_column: "pips_from_mid"`, one query
`{type: "stepArea", y_columns: ["bid_depth", "ask_depth"]}`.

**2. OHLC with a volume overlay that does not swamp the candles (500ms).**
Two statements: candles on the left axis, volume bars on the right axis.
Volume is normalised to 0.1..1 and the right axis is pinned to `0..4`, so the
bars use the bottom quarter of the chart.

```sql
SELECT timestamp, first(bids[1,1]) AS open, max(bids[1,1]) AS high,
       min(bids[1,1]) AS low, last(bids[1,1]) AS close
FROM market_data
WHERE timestamp >= dateadd('m', -1, @asof) AND timestamp <= @asof AND symbol = @symbol
SAMPLE BY 1s;
SELECT timestamp,
  0.1 + 0.9 * (total_volume - min(total_volume) OVER ())
      / NULLIF(max(total_volume) OVER () - min(total_volume) OVER (), 0) AS volume
FROM (
  SELECT timestamp, sum(bids[2,1]) AS total_volume FROM market_data
  WHERE timestamp >= dateadd('m', -1, @asof) AND timestamp <= @asof AND symbol = @symbol
  SAMPLE BY 1s
)
```
`queries`: `[{type: "candlestick", ohlc: {...}}, {type: "bar", y_columns: ["volume"], axis: "right", name: "Volume"}]`,
`right_axis: {name: "Volume (relative)", min: 0, max: 4}`.
(On consoles with candlestick `volume` support, a single query returning a
`volume` column is simpler.)

**3. Indicators on one chart (30s).** Four statements: 15m candles,
cumulative VWAP from 1m candles (left axis), RSI (right axis pinned 0..100),
Bollinger bands (left axis). Intraday range:
`timestamp >= timestamp_floor('d', @asof) AND timestamp <= @asof`.
`right_axis: {name: "RSI %", min: 0, max: 100}`.

**4. Live tables with highlight rules (250-500ms).** Last 6 seconds of spread
and notional (`SAMPLE BY 1s ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 6`) with gradient fills;
top-of-book vs core price (`LIMIT -6` for the last rows, then
`ASOF JOIN market_data ON symbol` and `insertion_point(bids[2], bid_volume)`
to find the book level a quote's size reaches), with step colors on `Level`.

**5. BBO and mirrored volume (30s).** `bbo_1s` bid/ask/mid lines on the left;
`SAMPLE BY 30s` bid notional and **negated** ask notional on the right, so
buy and sell pressure sit above and below zero.

---

## Pattern: Instance Monitoring Dashboard

Built on `sys.metrics` and `sys.telemetry_wal` (see `monitoring.md` for
the columns and queries). Layout: a full-width markdown cell explaining how to
read the panels, then w=6 chart pairs. Default refresh `30s`, `15s` for the
most important, `1m` for slow gauges. Techniques:

- Counters become rates with `lag()` deltas, guarded against restarts:
  `sum(CASE WHEN d >= 0 THEN d ELSE 0 END) / nullif(sum(seconds), 0)`.
- One line per table with `partition_by_column: "table_name"` after
  `JOIN tables() t ON s.tableId = t.id`; exclude views with `NOT t.matView`.
- "Hot tables only": a CTE picks the top 5 by p95 over the last 5 minutes and
  joins back to the 2-hour series.
- Units in the cell name ("· p95 ms", "(GiB)", "/min"), conversions in SQL
  (`/1073741824.0`).

---

## Dashboard Checklist

1. `get_workspace_state`, then `get_tables` / `get_table_schema` for real column names.
2. `validate_query` every statement.
3. `create_notebook(label)`, then one `apply_notebook_state` with
   `layout_mode: "grid"`, `auto_refresh_default`, `variables`, and every cell
   (name, value, mode, chart_config, grid, view `"result"`, per-cell `auto_refresh`).
4. Check the `runs[]` in the response and fix any `ERROR:` statements
   (draw cells are not in `runs[]`; test their SQL with `run_query` first).
5. Tell the user the notebook is ready in a background tab and offer to open it
   (`activate_notebook` only if they say yes).
6. Mention they can export it (tab menu > Export) to share it as JSON.

1	# QuestDB Cookbook Recipe Index

3	Official recipes, each fetchable as markdown. Paths are relative to
4	`https://questdb.com/docs/`:
5	
6	```bash

8	curl -s "https://questdb.com/docs/llms.txt"        # every page with its .md URL
9	```
10	
11	Most recipes run against `demo.questdb.io` tables. Adapt table and column
12	names to the user's schema (see the mapping in `indicators.md`).
13	
14	## Analysing a Dataset
15	
16	When asked to find issues, anomalies or patterns without a specific question:

# QuestDB Cookbook Recipe Index

Official recipes, each fetchable as markdown. Paths are relative to
`https://questdb.com/docs/`:

```bash
curl -s "https://questdb.com/docs/cookbook/sql/finance/markout.md"
curl -s "https://questdb.com/docs/llms.txt"        # every page with its .md URL
```

Most recipes run against `demo.questdb.io` tables. Adapt table and column
names to the user's schema (see the mapping in `indicators.md`).

## Analysing a Dataset

When asked to find issues, anomalies or patterns without a specific question:

0. Go wide before going deep, even when the prompt points at one topic.
   Profile every table in one query:
   `SELECT table_name, table_type, designatedTimestamp, table_row_count, table_min_timestamp, table_max_timestamp, dedup FROM tables() ORDER BY table_name`
   (views show no counts). Then give each table, including reference, master
   and configuration data (marks, instruments, limits, fees), one sanity check
   against the data it describes before any single method takes over the
   run. Keep this pass to a fraction of the queries you expect to run. Use
   the full time range the data covers for every finding, and state the
   window in the report; narrow it only when a question needs it.
1. Profile first: list every table's columns with
   `SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns`,
   then row counts, time span, gaps, nulls (`count() - count(col)`),
   duplicates per key, and late or restated rows.
2. Look for gaps at a resolution finer than the gap. Per source, measure the
   time between rows (`ts - lag(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY ts)`,
   in the timestamp's unit, since `datediff()` truncates to whole units), or
   count rows with `SAMPLE BY 10s FROM ... TO ... FILL(0)` and flag buckets
   far below that source's normal rate. Coarse buckets with a fixed
   threshold hide short outages. Start on a bounded window: a window function
   over a full day of a busy feed is slow.
3. Break each metric down by every categorical column in the schema, and by
   pairs of them. An effect concentrated in one segment can vanish in the
   average of a mix. When single values of a key are too sparse to show
   anything, group them by a derived attribute (a name prefix or pattern, a
   lookup table, size or activity tiers): the grouping that matters may not
   be a column. Start from the coarsest grouping that shows the effect, and
   split further only to explain it, while each cell keeps enough rows to
   judge. If a finer split leaves cells too small, report the coarser
   group's result rather than dropping it.
4. Match time scales to the data. Derive horizons and bucket sizes from the
   gaps between events and how long orders or positions live, and compare
   several scales instead of stopping at a default.
5. Separate common moves from specific ones. Before blaming one entity
   (counterparty, venue, device, host), check whether the whole population
   moved at the same time, against a benchmark or its peers.
6. Weigh the evidence. A thin cell first gets more data: widen the time range
   if history exists, or regroup as in step 3. An effect that holds across
   days, sides and horizons is stronger than one cell, and with many segments
   a few look significant by chance.
7. Report each finding with its size, the rows and period it affects, and the
   query that shows it. Never drop a signal for being underpowered: list it as
   a hypothesis with its `n` and t-statistic, and say what data would confirm
   it. Rank confirmed findings first. End with a coverage table: every table,
   what was checked, and the result ("checked, nothing found" counts), so a
   table that was never examined shows as a gap.

## Finance: Post-Trade and Execution Quality (TCA)

### Method

Work through the questions in order; each recipe below answers one:

1. **Slippage**: what did I pay? Fill price against mid (includes half the
   spread) and against top of book (beyond the spread), with the spread at
   fill time for context.
2. **Markout**: what happened next? Mid at offsets after each fill.
3. **Implementation shortfall**: why? Effective spread = permanent impact
   (mid at a settle horizon minus mid at fill) + temporary impact (the part
   that reverted).
4. **Scorecards**: where and with whom? The same metrics by venue,
   counterparty, passive/aggressive, side, size bucket and hour of day.
5. **Flow toxicity**: who is informed? VPIN, from volume imbalance rather than
   price.

Conventions the recipes share:
- Sign by side so positive markout means the market moved in your favour:
  `CASE t.side WHEN 'buy' THEN mid - t.price ELSE t.price - mid END`. Offset 0
  is then minus the slippage against mid.
- bps relative to the fill price (`/ t.price * 10000`). Report P&L in currency
  (`signed_diff * t.quantity`) and volume next to every bps figure: a bad
  markout on little volume may not matter. Volume-weighted bps:
  `sum(signed_diff * qty) / sum(t.price * qty) * 10000`.
- Read aggressive fills against the half-spread
  (`(ask - bid) / mid * 10000 / 2`): a markout near minus the half-spread
  that recovers is the normal cost of crossing; one that keeps falling is
  adverse selection.
- Include negative offsets (`LIST (-30s, 0, 1s, 30s, 5m)`): a curve already
  moving before 0 means leakage or stale signals.
- Pick horizons from the flow: milliseconds for last look, seconds to
  minutes for electronic fills, minutes to hours for slow or voice flow, and a
  settle horizon for IS (5 to 30 minutes for liquid FX, longer for illiquid
  markets). `RANGE` for a curve, `LIST` for key points.
- Report `count()` per cell and a t-statistic,
  `markout_bps / (stddev_samp(markout) / sqrt(n))`, before calling a
  segment good or bad. Compute the aggregates in a CTE and the ratio in the
  outer query: an aggregate's alias cannot be reused in the same SELECT. A segment that looks bad but is not significant is a
  hypothesis to report with its `n`, not a result to drop (see step 7 of
  Analysing a Dataset).
- Separate the segment from the market: compare its markout with all trades in
  the same symbol and period. A segment only stands out if it differs from
  that benchmark, not because the whole market moved. This last point is
  general TCA practice rather than one of the recipes.

```sql
-- Markout scorecard: one pass, every horizon; swap the GROUP BY columns
SELECT t.ecn, t.passive, h.offset / 1_000_000_000 AS horizon_sec,
       count() AS n, sum(t.quantity) AS volume,
       avg(CASE t.side WHEN 'buy' THEN (m.best_bid + m.best_ask) / 2 - t.price
                       ELSE t.price - (m.best_bid + m.best_ask) / 2 END
           / t.price * 10000) AS markout_bps,
       sum(CASE t.side WHEN 'buy' THEN (m.best_bid + m.best_ask) / 2 - t.price
                       ELSE t.price - (m.best_bid + m.best_ask) / 2 END
           * t.quantity) AS pnl,
       avg((m.best_ask - m.best_bid) / ((m.best_bid + m.best_ask) / 2) * 10000) / 2
           AS half_spread_bps
FROM fx_trades t
HORIZON JOIN market_data m ON (symbol)
LIST (-30s, 0, 1s, 30s, 5m) AS h
WHERE t.symbol = 'EURUSD' AND t.timestamp IN '$now-1h..$now'
ORDER BY t.ecn, t.passive, horizon_sec;
```

### Recipes

All built on `HORIZON JOIN`; use them instead of hand-rolled ASOF self-joins.

|--------|------|
| Post-trade analysis overview (start here) | `cookbook/sql/finance/post-trade-overview.md` |
| Slippage per fill | `cookbook/sql/finance/slippage.md` |
| Slippage aggregated by venue and counterparty | `cookbook/sql/finance/slippage-aggregated.md` |
| Markout (reversion, adverse selection) | `cookbook/sql/finance/markout.md` |
| Last-look detection (ms markouts) | `cookbook/sql/finance/last-look.md` |
| Implementation shortfall decomposition | `cookbook/sql/finance/implementation-shortfall.md` |
| Order-level implementation shortfall | `cookbook/sql/finance/implementation-shortfall-order.md` |
| ECN scorecard (pivoted) | `cookbook/sql/finance/ecn-scorecard.md` |

CREATE VIEW 'energy_positions_running_day' AS ( 
DECLARE OVERRIDABLE @day := timestamp_floor('d', now())
                SELECT ts, book, symbol, curve, venue, qty, px,
                       sum(qty)      OVER (PARTITION BY book, symbol ORDER BY ts)        AS pos,
                       sum(qty * px) OVER (PARTITION BY book, symbol ORDER BY ts)        AS cost,
                       sum(qty)      OVER (PARTITION BY book, symbol, venue ORDER BY ts) AS venue_pos
                FROM energy_fills
                WHERE ts >= @day::timestamp AND ts < dateadd('d', 1, @day::timestamp)
);

# Execution quality · Wednesday 11 Nov 2026 (session = `@day`)
Sign convention: **positive = market moved in our favour after the fill**, negative = against us. Slippage = markout at offset 0 (aggressive fills pay about the half-spread, passive fills earn it). Markouts are mid on the fill's own venue at +1m/+5m/+15m; `*_usd` columns are the mark-to-market of the day's fills at that horizon. Change `day` / `prev_day` / `spike` in the Variables popover to reuse tomorrow (e.g. `'$yesterday'`).

## Findings for 11 Nov 2026
1. **Yes, we were picked off, and it was concentrated in one episode.** The gas complex (NBP, TTF, JKM, UK power) rallied 3–4% in a near-straight line from **09:30 to 09:50 UTC** (NBP_Dec-26 206 → 222 p/th, settlement 219.3 vs 203.0 the day before, so the move is real). From 09:00 the desk was a heavy net **seller** of NBP (-3.9M therms 09:00–09:40) and about 60% of that was **passive offers that were lifted as the market ran through them** (trader_10, trader_13, trader_11, trader_20). 30-minute markout of NBP + UK power sells in 09:00–10:00: about **-$330k**. See the spike chart and fills table below.
2. **Outside the spike, the exchange flow is clean.** Aggressive fills pay ≈ the half-spread on every venue (CME 0.95 vs 0.93 bps, ICE 1.21 vs 1.24, ICE Endex 1.27 vs 1.39, EEX 2.47 vs 2.51) and passive fills earn it. Oil (Brent/WTI) markouts are positive at 5–15 min on both styles. Ex-spike, NBP passive is flat (+0.5 bps at 5m, t = 0.3).
3. **Persistent, smaller problems:** UK power aggressive fills on ICE are -6.0 bps at 5m ex-spike (n = 86, t = -3.1), driven by trader_19 and trader_20; Gasoil (PRODUCTS book, 100% aggressive, traders 05–08) pays 1.5 bps with no reversion, i.e. pure spread cost on $420M/day.
4. **OTC / broker counterparties (2-day sample):** flow from **INDUSTRIAL_xx via brokers** (-4.6 bps at 5m, t = -3.8; -10.9 bps at 30m, t = -2.9) and **UTILITY_xx via OTC** (-5.5 bps at 5m, t = -3.9) moves against us right after the trade; BANK flow via brokers moves in our favour. Per name the samples are 3–14 trades, so treat the per-counterparty table as a watch-list (INDUSTRIAL_08, UTILITY_09/10, PRODUCER_05), not a verdict.
5. **Things that look wrong but are not execution problems:** (a) **EEX quotes are not independent of fills**: every EEX fill has a quote exactly 1 ns before it at the fill price, so EEX slippage is tautologically ±half-spread and its 0–5 s markouts are meaningless; EEX also had a 3-minute feed gap 08:45–08:48. (b) **Stale quotes on illiquid tenors** (quarters/seasons): 14 TTF fills and 7 UK power fills had a venue quote older than 60 s (max 15 min), which makes their row-level markouts noisy. (c) **Booking latency**: OTC trades were booked on average 5.4 h after trade time, 26 of 101 on the next day, 11 trades were amended/cancelled after the fact (2 price corrections) – a book-as-of/risk problem, not a fill-quality one.

WITH m AS (
  SELECT f.venue, f.passive, f.symbol, h.offset / 1000000000 AS horizon_s, count() AS n,
    sum(CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / f.px * 10000) AS sum_bps,
    sum(CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(f.qty)) AS pnl_local,
    sum(abs(f.qty) * f.px) AS notional_local,
    sum((q.ask - q.bid) / (q.bid + q.ask) * 10000) AS sum_hs
  FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) LIST (0, 60s, 300s, 900s) AS h
  WHERE f.ts IN @day

# Execution quality · Wednesday 11 Nov 2026 (session = `@day`)
Sign convention: **positive = market moved in our favour after the fill**, negative = against us. Slippage = markout at offset 0 (aggressive fills pay about the half-spread, passive fills earn it). Markouts are mid on the fill's own venue at +1m/+5m/+15m; `*_usd` columns are the mark-to-market of the day's fills at that horizon. Change `day` / `prev_day` / `spike` in the Variables popover to reuse tomorrow (e.g. `'$yesterday'`).

## Findings for 11 Nov 2026
1. **Yes, we were picked off, and it was concentrated in one episode.** The gas complex (NBP, TTF, JKM, UK power) rallied 3–4% in a near-straight line from **09:30 to 09:50 UTC** (NBP_Dec-26 206 → 222 p/th, settlement 219.3 vs 203.0 the day before, so the move is real). From 09:00 the desk was a heavy net **seller** of NBP (-3.9M therms 09:00–09:40) and about 60% of that was **passive offers that were lifted as the market ran through them** (trader_10, trader_13, trader_11, trader_20). 30-minute markout of NBP + UK power sells in 09:00–10:00: about **-$330k**. See the spike chart and fills table below.
2. **Outside the spike, the exchange flow is clean.** Aggressive fills pay ≈ the half-spread on every venue (CME 0.95 vs 0.93 bps, ICE 1.21 vs 1.24, ICE Endex 1.27 vs 1.39, EEX 2.47 vs 2.51) and passive fills earn it. Oil (Brent/WTI) markouts are positive at 5–15 min on both styles. Ex-spike, NBP passive is flat (+0.5 bps at 5m, t = 0.3).
3. **Persistent, smaller problems:** UK power aggressive fills on ICE are -6.0 bps at 5m ex-spike (n = 86, t = -3.1), driven by trader_19 and trader_20; Gasoil (PRODUCTS book, 100% aggressive, traders 05–08) pays 1.5 bps with no reversion, i.e. pure spread cost on $420M/day.
4. **OTC / broker counterparties (2-day sample):** flow from **INDUSTRIAL_xx via brokers** (-4.6 bps at 5m, t = -3.8; -10.9 bps at 30m, t = -2.9) and **UTILITY_xx via OTC** (-5.5 bps at 5m, t = -3.9) moves against us right after the trade; BANK flow via brokers moves in our favour. Per name the samples are 3–14 trades, so treat the per-counterparty table as a watch-list (INDUSTRIAL_08, UTILITY_09/10, PRODUCER_05), not a verdict.
5. **Things that look wrong but are not execution problems:** (a) **EEX quotes are not independent of fills**: every EEX fill has a quote exactly 1 ns before it at the fill price, so EEX slippage is tautologically ±half-spread and its 0–5 s markouts are meaningless; EEX also had a 3-minute feed gap 08:45–08:48. (b) **Stale quotes on illiquid tenors** (quarters/seasons): 14 TTF fills and 7 UK power fills had a venue quote older than 60 s (max 15 min), which makes their row-level markouts noisy. (c) **Booking latency**: OTC trades were booked on average 5.4 h after trade time, 26 of 101 on the next day, 11 trades were amended/cancelled after the fact (2 price corrections) – a book-as-of/risk problem, not a fill-quality one.

FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source)
LIST (-60s, -5s, 0, 5s, 30s, 60s, 300s, 900s, 1800s) AS h
WHERE f.ts IN @day AND f.passive = false
ORDER BY horizon_s, f.venue

cells.name: Passive fills · markout curve by venue (bps vs horizon s)
cells.value:
SELECT h.offset / 1000000000 AS horizon_s, f.venue,
       round(avg(CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / f.px * 10000), 3) AS markout_bps
FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source)
LIST (-60s, -5s, 0, 5s, 30s, 60s, 300s, 900s, 1800s) AS h
WHERE f.ts IN @day AND f.passive = true
ORDER BY horizon_s, f.venue

cells.name: Curve scorecard · worst 15m mark-to-market first
cells.value:
WITH m AS (
  SELECT f.curve, f.passive, f.symbol, h.offset / 1000000000 AS horizon_s, count() AS n,
    sum(CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / f.px * 10000) AS sum_bps,
    sum(CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(f.qty)) AS pnl_local
  FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) LIST (0, 300s, 900s) AS h
  WHERE f.ts IN @day
), j AS (
  SELECT m.curve, m.passive, m.horizon_s, sum(m.n) AS n, sum(m.sum_bps) / sum(m.n) AS avg_bps, sum(m.pnl_local * u.factor) AS pnl_usd
  FROM m JOIN energy_usd_factor_asof u ON u.symbol = m.symbol
)
SELECT curve, CASE WHEN passive THEN 'passive' ELSE 'aggressive' END AS style, max(n) AS fills,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 0 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS slippage_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 300 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_5m_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 900 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_15m_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 300 THEN pnl_usd ELSE 0 END)) AS markout_5m_usd,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 900 THEN pnl_usd ELSE 0 END)) AS markout_15m_usd
FROM j ORDER BY markout_15m_usd

cells.name: 5-minute markout by hour of day (bps, UTC)
cells.value:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT hour(f.ts) AS hr, f.passive,
    CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / f.px * 10000 AS bps
  FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) LIST (300s) AS h
  WHERE f.ts IN @day
)
SELECT hr AS hour_utc, round(avg(CASE WHEN passive = false THEN bps END), 2) AS aggressive_5m_bps, round(avg(CASE WHEN passive THEN bps END), 2) AS passive_5m_bps, count() AS fills
FROM r ORDER BY hr

cells.name: The 09:30 gas rally · front-month move (bps from 08:00) vs our NBP net flow (M therms / 5 min)
cells.value:
WITH q AS (
  SELECT ts, symbol, close FROM energy_quotes_1m
  WHERE ts IN @spike AND symbol IN ('NBP_Dec-26', 'TTF_Dec-26', 'UKPWR_Jan-27', 'JKM_Jan-27', 'BRENT_Jan-27')
)
SELECT ts, symbol, round((close / first_value(close) OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY ts) - 1) * 10000, 1) AS move_bps
FROM q ORDER BY ts;
SELECT ts, sum(qty) / 1000000.0 AS nbp_net_flow_mtherm FROM energy_fills WHERE ts IN @spike AND curve = 'NBP' SAMPLE BY 5m FILL(0)

cells.name: Fills in the spike window (NBP / UK power / TTF) with 15m and 30m markouts
cells.value:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT f.trade_id, f.ts, f.symbol, f.venue, f.trader, f.passive, f.qty, f.px, (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 AS mid_15m
  FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) LIST (15m) AS h
  WHERE f.ts IN @spike AND f.curve IN ('NBP', 'UKPWR', 'TTF')
), b AS (
  SELECT f.trade_id, (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 AS mid_30m
  FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) LIST (30m) AS h
  WHERE f.ts IN @spike AND f.curve IN ('NBP', 'UKPWR', 'TTF')
)
SELECT a.ts, a.symbol, a.venue, a.trader, CASE WHEN a.passive THEN 'passive' ELSE 'aggressive' END AS style,
       CASE WHEN a.qty > 0 THEN 'buy' ELSE 'sell' END AS side, abs(a.qty) AS qty, a.px,
       round(CASE WHEN a.qty > 0 THEN a.mid_15m - a.px ELSE a.px - a.mid_15m END / a.px * 10000, 1) AS markout_15m_bps,
       round(CASE WHEN a.qty > 0 THEN b.mid_30m - a.px ELSE a.px - b.mid_30m END / a.px * 10000, 1) AS markout_30m_bps
FROM a JOIN b ON a.trade_id = b.trade_id ORDER BY a.ts

cells.name: Trader scorecard · worst 15m mark-to-market first
cells.value:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT f.trader, f.book, f.passive, f.symbol, h.offset / 1000000000 AS horizon_s,
    CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / f.px * 10000 AS bps,
    CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(f.qty) AS pnl_local
  FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) LIST (0, 300s, 900s) AS h
  WHERE f.ts IN @day
), a AS (
  SELECT r.trader, r.book, r.passive, r.horizon_s, count() AS n, avg(r.bps) AS avg_bps, stddev_samp(r.bps) AS sd, sum(r.pnl_local * u.factor) AS pnl_usd
  FROM r JOIN energy_usd_factor_asof u ON u.symbol = r.symbol
)
SELECT trader, book, CASE WHEN passive THEN 'passive' ELSE 'aggressive' END AS style, max(n) AS fills,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 0 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS slippage_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 300 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_5m_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 300 THEN avg_bps / (sd / sqrt(n)) ELSE 0 END), 1) AS t_stat_5m,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 900 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_15m_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 300 THEN pnl_usd ELSE 0 END)) AS markout_5m_usd,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 900 THEN pnl_usd ELSE 0 END)) AS markout_15m_usd
FROM a ORDER BY markout_15m_usd

cells.name: OTC / broker counterparties · price vs primary-venue screen mid at trade time (session)
cells.value:
WITH t AS ((SELECT trade_id, trade_ts, symbol, curve, counterparty, channel, qty, px FROM (SELECT * FROM energy_trade_events WHERE trade_ts IN @day AND channel != 'EXCH' LATEST ON booked_ts PARTITION BY trade_id) WHERE status != 'CANCELLED' ORDER BY trade_ts) timestamp(trade_ts)),
r1 AS (
  SELECT t.counterparty, t.channel, t.symbol, h.offset / 1000000 AS horizon_s,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / t.px * 10000 AS bps,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(t.qty) AS pnl_local
  FROM t HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (t.symbol = q.symbol AND q.source = 'ICE') LIST (0, 5m, 30m, 2h) AS h
  WHERE t.curve NOT IN ('WTI', 'TTF', 'EUA')
), r2 AS (
  SELECT t.counterparty, t.channel, t.symbol, h.offset / 1000000 AS horizon_s,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / t.px * 10000 AS bps,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(t.qty) AS pnl_local
  FROM t HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (t.symbol = q.symbol AND q.source = 'ICE_ENDEX') LIST (0, 5m, 30m, 2h) AS h
  WHERE t.curve IN ('TTF', 'EUA')
), r3 AS (
  SELECT t.counterparty, t.channel, t.symbol, h.offset / 1000000 AS horizon_s,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / t.px * 10000 AS bps,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(t.qty) AS pnl_local
  FROM t HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (t.symbol = q.symbol AND q.source = 'CME') LIST (0, 5m, 30m, 2h) AS h
  WHERE t.curve = 'WTI'
), r AS (SELECT * FROM r1 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM r2 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM r3),
a AS (
  SELECT r.counterparty, r.horizon_s, count() AS n, avg(r.bps) AS avg_bps, stddev_samp(r.bps) AS sd, sum(r.pnl_local * u.factor) AS pnl_usd
  FROM r JOIN energy_usd_factor_asof u ON u.symbol = r.symbol
)
SELECT counterparty, max(n) AS trades,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 0 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS slippage_vs_screen_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 300 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_5m_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 1800 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_30m_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 1800 THEN avg_bps / (sd / sqrt(n)) ELSE 0 END), 1) AS t_stat_30m,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 7200 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_2h_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 1800 THEN pnl_usd ELSE 0 END)) AS markout_30m_usd
FROM a ORDER BY markout_30m_usd

cells.name: Counterparty type × channel · markouts over @cpty_window (more trades per cell)
cells.value:
WITH t AS ((SELECT trade_id, trade_ts, symbol, curve, channel, qty, px, regexp_replace(counterparty, '_[0-9]+$', '') AS cpty_type FROM (SELECT * FROM energy_trade_events WHERE trade_ts IN @cpty_window AND channel != 'EXCH' LATEST ON booked_ts PARTITION BY trade_id) WHERE status != 'CANCELLED' ORDER BY trade_ts) timestamp(trade_ts)),
r1 AS (
  SELECT t.cpty_type, t.channel, t.symbol, h.offset / 1000000 AS horizon_s,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / t.px * 10000 AS bps,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(t.qty) AS pnl_local
  FROM t HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (t.symbol = q.symbol AND q.source = 'ICE') LIST (0, 5m, 30m, 2h) AS h
  WHERE t.curve NOT IN ('WTI', 'TTF', 'EUA')
), r2 AS (
  SELECT t.cpty_type, t.channel, t.symbol, h.offset / 1000000 AS horizon_s,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / t.px * 10000 AS bps,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(t.qty) AS pnl_local
  FROM t HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (t.symbol = q.symbol AND q.source = 'ICE_ENDEX') LIST (0, 5m, 30m, 2h) AS h
  WHERE t.curve IN ('TTF', 'EUA')
), r3 AS (
  SELECT t.cpty_type, t.channel, t.symbol, h.offset / 1000000 AS horizon_s,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / t.px * 10000 AS bps,
    CASE WHEN t.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - t.px ELSE t.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END * abs(t.qty) AS pnl_local
  FROM t HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (t.symbol = q.symbol AND q.source = 'CME') LIST (0, 5m, 30m, 2h) AS h
  WHERE t.curve = 'WTI'
), r AS (SELECT * FROM r1 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM r2 UNION ALL SELECT * FROM r3),
a AS (
  SELECT r.cpty_type, r.channel, r.horizon_s, count() AS n, avg(r.bps) AS avg_bps, stddev_samp(r.bps) AS sd, sum(r.pnl_local * u.factor) AS pnl_usd
  FROM r JOIN energy_usd_factor_asof u ON u.symbol = r.symbol
)
SELECT cpty_type, channel, max(n) AS trades,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 0 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS slippage_vs_screen_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 300 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_5m_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 300 THEN avg_bps / (sd / sqrt(n)) ELSE 0 END), 1) AS t_stat_5m,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 1800 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_30m_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 1800 THEN avg_bps / (sd / sqrt(n)) ELSE 0 END), 1) AS t_stat_30m,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 7200 THEN avg_bps ELSE 0 END), 2) AS markout_2h_bps,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN horizon_s = 1800 THEN pnl_usd ELSE 0 END)) AS markout_30m_usd
FROM a ORDER BY cpty_type, channel

cells.name: Day over day · 5m markout by venue (@day vs @prev_day)
cells.value:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT 'current' AS which, f.venue, f.passive, count() AS n,
    avg(CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / f.px * 10000) AS bps
  FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) LIST (300s) AS h
  WHERE f.ts IN @day
), p AS (
  SELECT 'previous' AS which, f.venue, f.passive, count() AS n,
    avg(CASE WHEN f.qty > 0 THEN (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 - f.px ELSE f.px - (q.bid + q.ask) / 2 END / f.px * 10000) AS bps
  FROM energy_fills f HORIZON JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) LIST (300s) AS h
  WHERE f.ts IN @prev_day
)
SELECT r.venue, CASE WHEN r.passive THEN 'passive' ELSE 'aggressive' END AS style, r.n AS fills_today, round(r.bps, 2) AS markout_5m_today, p.n AS fills_prev, round(p.bps, 2) AS markout_5m_prev, round(r.bps - p.bps, 2) AS change_bps
FROM r JOIN p ON r.venue = p.venue AND r.passive = p.passive ORDER BY r.venue, style

cells.name: Data quality · age of the venue quote at fill time (stale quotes = noisy markouts)
cells.value:
WITH r AS (SELECT f.venue, f.curve, (f.ts - q.ts) / 1000000000.0 AS age_s FROM energy_fills f ASOF JOIN energy_quotes q ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source) WHERE f.ts IN @day)
SELECT venue, curve, count() AS fills, round(avg(age_s), 2) AS avg_quote_age_s, round(max(age_s), 1) AS max_quote_age_s,
       sum(CASE WHEN age_s > 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fills_quote_older_10s, sum(CASE WHEN age_s > 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fills_quote_older_60s
FROM r ORDER BY max_quote_age_s DESC

cells.name: Data quality · booking latency by channel (trade_ts → booked_ts)
cells.value:
SELECT channel, count() AS trades, round(avg(datediff('m', trade_ts, booked_ts)), 0) AS avg_booking_lag_min, max(datediff('m', trade_ts, booked_ts)) AS max_booking_lag_min,
       sum(CASE WHEN datediff('m', trade_ts, booked_ts) > 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS booked_over_1h_late,
       sum(CASE WHEN timestamp_floor('d', booked_ts) > timestamp_floor('d', trade_ts) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS booked_next_day
FROM energy_trade_events WHERE trade_ts IN @day AND status = 'NEW' ORDER BY channel

cells.name: Data quality · quote feed gaps per source (1-minute buckets)
cells.value:
SELECT source, min(n) AS min_quotes_per_min, round(avg(n)) AS avg_quotes_per_min, sum(CASE WHEN n = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS empty_minutes
FROM (SELECT ts, source, count() AS n FROM energy_quotes WHERE ts IN @day SAMPLE BY 1m FILL(0)) ORDER BY source

cells.name: Amended and cancelled trades (latest version differs from the original booking)
cells.value:
SELECT e.booked_ts, e.trade_ts, e.status, e.reason, e.symbol, e.channel, e.counterparty, e.trader, e.qty, e.px, e.version, e.booked_by
FROM energy_trade_events e WHERE e.trade_ts IN @day AND e.version > 1 ORDER BY e.booked_ts

---
name: energy-desk-questdb-schema
description: Non-obvious conventions of the user's energy-trading QuestDB (fills sign, per-venue quotes, EEX quote artifact, OTC trades only in trade_events) and the TCA dashboard built on 2026-11-12
metadata:
  type: project
---

The user runs an energy trading desk; their QuestDB holds `energy_*` tables (fills, trade_events, quotes, instruments, listings, marks, settlements).

- `energy_fills.qty` is signed (positive = buy); there is no side column. Exchange fills only (ICE, ICE_ENDEX, CME, EEX).
- OTC/BROKER trades exist only in `energy_trade_events` (versioned: use `LATEST ON booked_ts PARTITION BY trade_id`, drop CANCELLED). Counterparty lives there; exchange rows carry the CCP.
- `energy_quotes.source` is the venue; join fills to quotes with `ON (f.symbol = q.symbol AND f.venue = q.source)` (works in HORIZON JOIN). Primary venues: WTI→CME, TTF/EUA→ICE_ENDEX, rest→ICE.
- EEX quotes are not independent of fills: every EEX fill has a quote 1 ns earlier at the fill price, so EEX offset-0 metrics are tautological.
- USD conversion: `energy_usd_factor_asof` view (symbol → factor); NBP is in pence (px_factor 0.01).
- Selecting a bare `version` column resolves to the version() function; alias the table (`e.version`).
- Dashboard "Execution Quality – 2026-11-11" (Web Console notebook, variables day/prev_day/spike/cpty_window) was built on 2026-11-12 for the 2026-11-11 session.

**Why:** these cost several wrong queries to discover and are not documented in the schema.
**How to apply:** reuse the join pattern and version handling for any TCA work; change the notebook variables rather than rebuilding it.
